newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hamanaka had secret office for LME trades - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hamanaka had secret office for LME trades - paper.

text.p: Former Sumitomo Corp copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka traded on the London metal market from a private apartment he rented in Tokyo, a Japanese newspaper reported on Friday.

The Yomiuri Shimbun said Hamanaka, who has been arrested on suspicion of forging documents related to Sumitomo's huge losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), used the apartment as a "secret office" for trading on the London metal market during the Japanese nighttime.
The newspaper did not specify its source in the report.
An official at the prosecutors' office said he could not comment on any individual case.
Tokyo prosecutors on Tuesday arrested Hamanaka on suspicion of forging the signatures of his superiors on trading authority documents.
Sumitomo says Hamanaka, who was fired in mid-June, had conducted unauthorised trades that led to losses estimated at $2.6 billion on the world copper market.
The Japanese daily also said Tokyo prosecutors had already raided the apartment and obtained some trading documents.
Hamanaka is being held at a detention centre in Tokyo and cannot be reached for comment on the case.
